{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"The red bicycle was missing its front wheel. Mara found it leaning against the fence behind her grandfather’s shed, its handlebars turned toward the road as if it had tried to leave without her. She had ridden it every summer since she was tall enough to reach the pedals. Now rust freckled the chain, and the back tire had gone soft.

She opened the shed, expecting to find the wheel among the jars of screws and broken garden tools. Instead, she found a note pinned above the workbench: Ask Mr. Bell about the parade.

Mr. Bell lived three houses down. When Mara knocked, he led her to his garage, where the wheel hung from a nail. Paper stars, faded blue and gold, were still caught between its spokes.

“Your grandfather lent it to me,” he said. “My grandson wanted to build a little cart for the parade. We never finished it.”

Mara turned the wheel gently. It spun without a wobble. She remembered her grandfather running beside her on the first day she rode without training wheels, one hand hovering near the seat long after he had let go.

Mr. Bell offered to help put the bicycle back together. They carried the wheel across the street and worked until the axle sat snugly in its fork. Mara pumped up the tires while he tightened the brakes.

By evening, the bicycle was ready. Mara rode it once around the block, slowly at first, then fast enough for the wind to lift her hair. When she passed the shed, she rang the bell twice."}
